name: SubDL Scribe
description: SubDL Scribe brings SubDL.com to Jellyfin: it downloads missing subtitles for the languages and libraries you pick and uploads your own. Download is on by default; upload is off — enable at your choice. Requires a SubDL login and API Key plus a TMDb API Key.
overview: Sync subtitles with SubDL — download missing and upload new subtitles.

versions.changelog:
v12.1.12.159: The refresh chapters and the dry-run report.
    The download dry run reported a file name it cannot know. Its report ends before the
    fetch by design, but a second log site further down printed the name with the
    hearing-impaired marker and the byte size - and sat after the dry run's own break, so it
    never ran at all. A dry run holds no bytes and never builds a name from a fetched file,
    so the site is removed and the wording follows: a dry run answers WHICH RELEASE per
    language, not WHICH FILE. The same wording was corrected on the settings page.
    The database refresh and the OSHash refresh each state their own procedure now, in one
    place instead of spread over their chapters. Eleven rules whose code anchors live in
    other components (counters, log levels, the configuration page, the reset UI, the
    registry hash, the data model) moved to the chapter they belong to, so a chapter
    describes its own task again.
    The database refresh no longer drops download marks it cannot see, and it checks the
    hearing-impaired variant. A dry run no longer marks the files it reports as complete -
    a run against a library used to leave that library marked as done, so the next real run
    skipped the very files the dry run had been asked to report.
